titleEn: Asking a neighbor to keep the noise down
titleTh: ขอให้เพื่อนบ้านลดเสียงดังตอนกลางคืน
scenarioSentences: You live in a small apartment.
Your neighbor Carlos plays loud music late.
You have exams next week.
You are not sleeping well.
You knock on his door politely.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi Carlos, sorry to bother you. Do you have a minute?

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.text: Sure. Is something wrong?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Your music is quite loud at night. I can hear it through the wall.

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't realize the walls were so thin.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's usually fine, but I have exams next week and need more sleep.

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.text: I understand. I've been practicing for a band concert.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could you stop playing by ten o'clock on weeknights?

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.text: That's fair. I'll use headphones after ten.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thank you so much. Good luck with your concert!

dialogue.speaker: Carlos
dialogue.text: Thanks. Tell me if it's still too loud.

titleEn: Discussing shifts for a café job
titleTh: คุยเรื่องกะงานร้านกาแฟ
scenarioSentences: You applied for a part-time café job.
Ms. Novak is the café manager.
She wants to discuss your shifts.
You have classes every Tuesday.
You meet her at the café.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi Ms. Novak. I'd like to talk about my shifts.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Novak
dialogue.text: Of course. Which days can you work?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'm free on weekends, but I have classes all day on Tuesdays.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Novak
dialogue.text: That's fine. We're busiest on Saturdays and Sundays anyway.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How long would each shift be?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Novak
dialogue.text: Six hours, from eight until two. Have you made coffee before?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not in a café, but I've worked in a restaurant kitchen.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Novak
dialogue.text: Then let's do a trial shift this Saturday. Can you come at eight?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, I can. Should I bring anything?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Novak
dialogue.text: Just wear black shoes. We'll give you the rest.

titleTh: หารค่าไฟกับรูมเมต
scenarioSentences: You share an apartment with Priya.
The electricity bill is much higher this month.
You usually split the bill equally.
You think you know the reason.
You talk to Priya at dinner.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Priya, have you seen the electricity bill? It's almost double this month.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Really? I haven't checked it yet. How much is it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's ninety dollars. Last month it was only fifty.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Oh no. I think it's my heater. I've used it every night.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That might be it. It's been really cold.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Should I pay more this time?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Maybe we could split it by use instead of half and half.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: That's fair. What if I pay sixty and you pay thirty?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sounds good. Let's compare the next bill too.

dialogue.speaker: Priya
dialogue.text: Okay. I'll try to use the heater less.

titleTh: ได้ของที่สั่งออนไลน์ผิดสี
scenarioSentences: You ordered a lamp online last week.
It arrived this morning.
You wanted a white lamp, but it's green.
Mr. Evans works in customer service.
You call him about the problem.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, I'm calling because I received the wrong lamp.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Evans
dialogue.text: I'm sorry about that. What exactly happened?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I ordered a white lamp, but a green one arrived this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Evans
dialogue.text: I can see our mistake here. Would you like a refund or a new lamp?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'd prefer a white lamp. How long will delivery take?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Evans
dialogue.text: About three days. I'll email you a free return label today.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. Should I send the green one back first?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Evans
dialogue.text: No, you can send it anytime this month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. Thanks for sorting it out so quickly.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Evans
dialogue.text: You're welcome. Sorry again for the trouble.

titleTh: ตกรถไฟเที่ยวสุดท้าย
scenarioSentences: You are out with your friend Jake.
You stayed too late at a concert.
The last train has already left.
You both live far away.
You need another way home.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Jake, I think we've missed the last train.

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: Oh no. What should we do now?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: We could share a taxi, or we could wait for the night bus.

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: A taxi would be faster. How much would it cost?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Probably around forty dollars. That's too expensive for me.

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: Me too. When does the night bus come?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: There's one every thirty minutes. The next one comes in twenty minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: It's slower, but it's much cheaper. Let's take it together.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good idea. The stop is just across the street.

dialogue.speaker: Jake
dialogue.text: Let's go now so we don't miss this one too.

titleTh: วางแผนงานวันเกิดเซอร์ไพรส์
scenarioSentences: Your friend Mei's birthday is next Friday.
You want to plan a surprise party.
Hana is Mei's close friend too.
You meet Hana after class.
You ask for her help.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hana, Mei's birthday is next Friday. Should we plan a surprise party?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: I love that idea! Where could we have it?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: My room is too small, and restaurants are expensive.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: We could use my apartment. It has a big living room.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Perfect. How many people should we invite?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Maybe twelve. If everyone brings food, we'll spend less.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good idea. I can buy the cake and decorations.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Sounds fun. But how do we keep it secret?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll invite Mei to watch a movie at your place.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Nice. She'll never guess!

titleTh: ขอพักสมาชิกฟิตเนสชั่วคราว
scenarioSentences: You have a gym membership.
You're traveling for all of next month.
Ms. Reed works at the gym desk.
You ask her about your options.
You don't want to cancel.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi Ms. Reed. I'm traveling next month. Can I pause my membership?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Reed
dialogue.text: Yes, you can freeze it. How long will you be away?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Exactly four weeks. I leave on the first.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Reed
dialogue.text: That's fine. Freezing costs a small fee of ten dollars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's cheaper than a whole month. What about my locker?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Reed
dialogue.text: You can keep it, but you have to empty it first.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No problem. Do I need to fill in a form?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Reed
dialogue.text: Yes, just sign here. Your payments will start again after four weeks.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks a lot. See you when I get back.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Reed
dialogue.text: Have a good trip!

titleTh: ซ่อมจอแล็ปท็อปที่แตก
scenarioSentences: You dropped your laptop this morning.
Now its screen is cracked.
You use it for all your homework.
Mr. Okafor fixes computers on campus.
You bring the laptop to him.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Mr. Okafor. I dropped my laptop and the screen cracked. Can you repair it?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Okafor
dialogue.text: Let me look. Yes, we can replace the screen.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How much will it cost?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Okafor
dialogue.text: It's eighty, with the campus discount.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's okay. How long will the repair take?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Okafor
dialogue.text: About seven days. We have to order a new screen.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Seven days? I have an essay due on Thursday.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Okafor
dialogue.text: Don't worry. You can borrow one of our laptops until yours is fixed.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's so helpful. Should I return it when I collect mine?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Okafor
dialogue.text: Exactly. Just leave your phone number so we can call you.

titleTh: เลือกระหว่างอพาร์ตเมนต์สองแห่ง
scenarioSentences: You are looking for a new apartment.
You have found two options.
One is cheap but far from campus.
Your friend Sofia has seen both.
You ask for her opinion.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sofia, I can't decide between the two apartments.

dialogue.speaker: Sofia
dialogue.text: The first one is cheaper. How far is it from campus?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It's about forty minutes by bike. The other one is only ten.

dialogue.speaker: Sofia
dialogue.text: Forty minutes is a long ride, especially when it rains.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: True, but the near one costs a hundred dollars more each month.

dialogue.speaker: Sofia
dialogue.text: Have you thought about bus fares if you can't cycle?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not really. That might cost almost as much.

dialogue.speaker: Sofia
dialogue.text: Then the near one is better. You'll save time too.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: You're right. I'll call the landlord and say yes today.

dialogue.speaker: Sofia
dialogue.text: Good luck with the move!

titleEn: Ordering food with a nut allergy
titleTh: สั่งอาหารเมื่อแพ้ถั่ว
scenarioSentences: You are having dinner at a restaurant.
You are allergic to nuts.
You want to order the chicken pasta.
Paolo is your waiter tonight.
You ask him about the sauce.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Excuse me. I have a nut allergy. Is the chicken pasta safe?

dialogue.speaker: Paolo
dialogue.text: I'm not sure. The sauce might have nuts.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Could you check with the kitchen? It's quite serious.

dialogue.speaker: Paolo
dialogue.text: Of course. Wait here, I'll ask the chef.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'll look at the menu while I wait.

dialogue.speaker: Paolo
dialogue.text: The chef says the sauce has nuts, so please don't order it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Good to know. Which dishes are safe for me?

dialogue.speaker: Paolo
dialogue.text: The grilled fish and the tomato soup have no nuts at all.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I'll have the grilled fish, then.

dialogue.speaker: Paolo
dialogue.text: Good choice. I'll tell the kitchen about your allergy too.

titleEn: Sharing a car for a weekend trip
titleTh: ติดรถเพื่อนไปเที่ยวสุดสัปดาห์
scenarioSentences: You and Ravi are classmates.
You are both going to the beach this weekend.
Ravi has a car.
You want to travel with him.
You discuss the plan after class.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Ravi, can I come with you to the beach on Saturday?

dialogue.speaker: Ravi
dialogue.text: Sure! It's a three-hour drive, so company would be nice.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Thanks. I'd like to pay for some of the gas.

dialogue.speaker: Ravi
dialogue.text: That's kind. Should we just split it fifty-fifty?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Sounds fair. I can also drive part of the way if you're tired.

dialogue.speaker: Ravi
dialogue.text: Great. You drive there, and I'll drive back.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: What time should we leave?

dialogue.speaker: Ravi
dialogue.text: Early, so we can avoid traffic. How about seven?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Seven is too early for me. Could we leave at eight instead?

dialogue.speaker: Ravi
dialogue.text: Okay, eight it is. I'll pick you up outside your dorm.

titleTh: จ่ายค่าปรับคืนหนังสือห้องสมุดช้า
scenarioSentences: You borrowed three books last month.
You forgot to return them on time.
Now you have a fine.
Mrs. Chen is the librarian.
You call to ask her about it.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Mrs. Chen. I got an email about a fine for three books.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Chen
dialogue.text: Yes, they're two weeks late. That's twelve dollars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Twelve dollars? Sorry, I completely forgot.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Chen
dialogue.text: It happens. Do you still have the books?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Yes, they're in my bag. I can bring them this afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Chen
dialogue.text: If you return them today, I can reduce the fine to five dollars.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That would be great. Can I pay by card?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Chen
dialogue.text: Yes, at the front desk. Please come before six o'clock.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I will. Could you remind me next time by text?

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Chen
dialogue.text: Of course. I'll add your phone number to your account.

titleTh: ช่วยเลี้ยงแมวให้เพื่อน
scenarioSentences: Your friend Emma is away next week.
She has a cat named Bean.
Bean is old and takes medicine.
Emma asks you to help.
You meet her at her apartment.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi Emma. So, what does Bean need while you're away?

dialogue.speaker: Emma
dialogue.text: Thanks for helping! She eats twice a day, at eight and at six.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Okay. How much food should I give her?

dialogue.speaker: Emma
dialogue.text: Half a cup each time, even if she asks for more.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Got it. You said she takes medicine, right?

dialogue.speaker: Emma
dialogue.text: Yes, one pill every morning. Hide it in a little cheese.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That sounds easy enough. Should I change her water too?

dialogue.speaker: Emma
dialogue.text: Yes, please. Fresh water every visit.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then I'll come twice a day, before class and after dinner.

dialogue.speaker: Emma
dialogue.text: Perfect. I'll leave the spare key with you tonight.

titleTh: จองเรียนขับรถ
scenarioSentences: You want to learn to drive.
You have never driven a car before.
Mr. Brooks is a driving instructor.
You call to ask about lessons.
You are free most evenings.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hello, Mr. Brooks. I'd like to book some driving lessons.

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Brooks
dialogue.text: Sure. Have you had any lessons before?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: No, I'm a complete beginner. How many lessons will I need?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Brooks
dialogue.text: Most beginners need about ten before the test.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And how much does each lesson cost?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Brooks
dialogue.text: Forty dollars an hour, or three hundred fifty for ten.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: The package is cheaper, so I'll take ten. When can we start?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Brooks
dialogue.text: I have evenings free next week. Is Monday at six okay?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Monday works for me. When could I take the test?

dialogue.speaker: Mr. Brooks
dialogue.text: If you practice well, you could book it for next month.

titleTh: สมัครเรียนปฐมพยาบาล
scenarioSentences: You want to learn first aid.
It will help with your summer job.
Ms. Cole organizes the courses.
You visit her office to ask.
You work during the week.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Hi, Ms. Cole. When does your next first-aid course start?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Cole
dialogue.text: There's an evening course this month and a weekend course next month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: I work on weekdays, so the weekend suits me. How long is it?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Cole
dialogue.text: Two full days, Saturday and Sunday, from nine to five.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: How much does it cost?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Cole
dialogue.text: It's sixty dollars, including the book and the lunch.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: That's not bad. Will I get a certificate at the end?

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Cole
dialogue.text: Yes, if you pass the short test on Sunday afternoon.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Great. Please put my name down for the weekend course.

dialogue.speaker: Ms. Cole
dialogue.text: Done. You can pay here before it starts.
